title: Use a module from outside
starter:
module Stack = struct
  type t = int list
  let empty = []
  let push x s = x :: s
  let pop s = match s with [] -> None | x :: rest -> Some (x, rest)
end

let push_all (xs : int list) (s : Stack.t) : Stack.t =
  s
hints: You are outside the module here, so `push` alone is an unbound value. Its full name is `Stack.push`.
Push the items one at a time, carrying the stack along. That is the job of `List.fold_left`, with the stack as the accumulator.
`List.fold_left (fun acc x -> Stack.push x acc) s xs`.

answer.code:
module Stack = struct
  type t = int list
  let empty = []
  let push x s = x :: s
  let pop s = match s with [] -> None | x :: rest -> Some (x, rest)
end

let push_all (xs : int list) (s : Stack.t) : Stack.t =
  List.fold_left (fun acc x -> Stack.push x acc) s xs
answer.explain: The reference is `List.fold_left (fun acc x -> Stack.push x acc) s xs`. Each step takes the stack so far and returns a taller one. Outside `struct ... end` the function is named `Stack.push`, the same way you write `List.map`. The first item is pushed first, so the last item ends up on top.
